items.title: Physical Data: The New Gold Rush
points: HANDO Labs created a crowdsourced data network where users record everyday tasks (fastening buckles, sorting objects) and receive tokenized stock exposure (fractional ownership rights represented digitally) to companies like Nvidia or Apple in exchange.
The model addresses a bottleneck: robots need massive amounts of labeled physical-world video data to learn manipulation tasks, and traditional data collection is expensive and slow.
The initiative garnered 1.2M views, showing market appetite for monetizing mundane activities and suggesting physical data could become a tradable commodity.

items.title: Humanoids Go Mainstream, But Market Reality Lags Hype
points: Global humanoid robot sales totaled just 7,000 units last year despite years of forecasts projecting millions, revealing a gap between investor enthusiasm and actual deployment.

Humanoid robot REK's 'Rekbot' defeated MMA fighter Frankie LaPenna in a viral San Francisco cage match promoted as a VR game event, showcasing robots' entertainment potential while raising safety questions.

Unitree robots danced at Vogue World Milan's 'Age of Intelligence' segment but drew backlash from fashion insiders over Silicon Valley's cultural encroachment, suggesting novelty alone won't sustain mainstream acceptance.
Chinese robotics firm AGIBOT deployed humanoids across 100+ locations at a theme park and delivered its 20,000th production robot.

items.title: Amazon's Robot Bet: Scale Over Innovation
points: Amazon is investing over $100M to build a 585,000-square-foot robotics manufacturing plant in Greenwood, Indiana, opening by 2028 with 300 jobs averaging $100,000 annually.
The company now operates over 1 million robots across 300+ facilities, supporting 75% of customer orders worldwide.
Amazon's expansion doubles its robot-making capacity alongside a new Texas facility, betting that supply-chain automation will remain a competitive advantage as labor costs persist.

items.title: Waymo's Autonomous Ride Scale
points: Waymo averages 500,000 paid autonomous rides weekly across 15 US cities, though 80% of its fleet remains concentrated in California and Texas.
